creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 8, item 2.

`len` is not checked when a list or variadic arg collects zero values:

```rad
args:
    *ports int    # At least one.
    ports len [1,]
```

```
$ ./s.rad
ports=[ ]
```

Nonzero counts are enforced (`len [2,2]` rejects 1 and 3), but `len [2,2]` also accepts zero, so the constraint appears to be skipped when the arg is treated as absent rather than empty. That is the case a lower bound exists for, and it is the failure the v0.12 list-constraint work (a_25c7AwONv, a_25c7On7dH) set out to end: a declared constraint that reads as validation and is not.

Confirmed on main (3459ddf1).

Where: len enforcement added in e3153393 (core/args.go / ra slice flag validation).
title: A len lower bound is skipped when a list arg receives no values
